ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper part of the image shows a sequence labeled mRNA, which can be read by triplets as AUG, CCA, CUA, GCA, CGU; the corresponding protein amino acid boxes below it are labeled in order as Met, Pro, Leu, Ala, Arg. The lower part of the image also gives a genetic code table, used to illustrate the correspondence between mRNA codons and amino acids. Reasoning: The problem asks for the DNA strand that can serve as the template for this amino acid sequence. According to the specified method, treat the mRNA shown in the figure as the transcription product, and write the DNA template strand that is complementary to it and antiparallel. The base pairing is: AUG corresponds to TAC, CCA corresponds to GGT, CUA corresponds to GAT, GCA corresponds to CGT, CGU corresponds to GCA. After merging, the direction of the DNA template strand is 3′ to 5′, namely 3′-TACGGTGATCGTGCA-5′.

raw_record.question_text: What DNA strand would serve as a template for the amino acid sequence shown above?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the upper diagram shows an mRNA sequence divided into codons AUG, CCA, CUA, GCA, and CGU, producing the protein sequence Met-Pro-Leu-Ala-Arg. Since the question asks for the DNA template strand, take the displayed mRNA as the transcript. Write the complementary DNA bases underneath in the opposite orientation: AUG -> TAC, CCA -> GGT, CUA -> GAT, GCA -> CGT, CGU -> GCA. Combine these codons and label the strand antiparallel to the mRNA as 3′-TACGGTGATCGTGCA-5′.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct visual-transcription route: it uses the mRNA sequence printed in the image rather than reconstructing possible codons from the amino-acid names. It is the natural single reliable route because the figure already shows the exact mRNA codons for the displayed protein.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the top mRNA strand in the image as 5′-AUG CCA CUA GCA CGU-3′, aligned with the protein labels Met, Pro, Leu, Ala, Arg. The codon table in the lower image can be used only as confirmation that these codons match the shown amino acids.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read the prompt as asking specifically for the DNA strand that serves as the template for the amino acid sequence shown above, not the coding DNA strand or the mRNA strand.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply base-pairing and antiparallel transcription rules: the DNA template is complementary to the mRNA and runs 3′ to 5′ opposite the mRNA. Pair A in mRNA with T in DNA, U with A, G with C, and C with G.
